paradoxes.text: The review that courts US investment examines Chinese deals that are still running, so the move meant to tie Honduras closer to Washington can cost the Chinese-funded projects the country still depends on. Our reading of the Bloomberg framing, confidence C.

sources.title: Honduras Reviews China Deals, Mulls Restoring Taiwan Ties

grand_strategy.reading: Honduras is a partner of both Washington and Beijing with no alignment to either, and since January 2026 its new president has reviewed the March 2023 switch to China rather than reversed it. The Taiwan question is open: a return to Taipei would undo that switch, and Asfura says the US tie, with its remittances, TPS and maquila jobs, comes first. The paradox sits in the review itself, which courts US investment by examining the Chinese deals the country still runs, so the check on Beijing may cost the projects that make Honduras worth courting.

stances.note: Transactional. Honduras shifted recognition to the People's Republic in March 2023 and broke with Taipei (the date is taken from the Taiwan card's sources). Under Asfura, in office since 27 January 2026, the government has reviewed the Castro-era agreements with Beijing, including Huawei telecom infrastructure, and Bloomberg reports it weighing the ties (May 2026). Grade partner and trend cooling are our reading, not a source's words: no source read calls the relation reluctant or hostile. No treaty ties the two states. Bond none: no shared identity and no open grievance. Confidence C because the grade and the trend are our reading; the review has no outcome by October 2026.

stances_toward.note: Partner, cooling with the change of government. Under Xiomara Castro the two presidents met in Mexico City in late November 2025 (energy, youth programmes, migration) and Honduras said it would renew its agreement with Pemex on oil exploration (Revista EyN); Sheinbaum asked that the will of the Honduran people be respected without outside intervention, days before the vote. The winner, Nasry Asfura of the National Party, was fully backed by Trump, and Mexican coverage notes the Pemex agreements could be at risk; people close to Asfura say he will work with Mexico despite a different ideology (Milenio). Honduras also supported the 3 Jan 2026 US strikes on Venezuela while Mexico condemned them (Fox News). Partner not rival: relations are intact and no source reads hostility. Bond none, our reading. Confidence C: no source of Asfura's own government on Mexico, and no date for Asfura's inauguration was read. Gap: the status of the Pemex contracts.

stances_toward.note: Taipei lost Honduras on 26 Mar 2023 and grades it neutral and warming: President Asfura campaigned on restoring ties, met Trump in Feb 2026, and has ordered a review of Castro-era agreements with China (including Huawei telecom infrastructure); Vice Foreign Minister Chen said in June that Taipei wants relations back 'as soon as possible' and is ready to reactivate programmes. Beijing reiterates One China. Asfura says he must protect the US relationship (remittances, TPS, maquila jobs) and 'it is not as simple as flipping a switch'. No decision found by October 2026. Bond - none.
